subject: Clarify processing regions, transit paths, and deletion policy for LedgerWorks POC
message_1_subject: Clarify processing regions, transit paths, and deletion policy for LedgerWorks POC
message_1_body:
Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — LedgerWorks is excited to move the POC forward. Before we spin up sample traffic, our security and privacy team needs a quick Q&A on where data is processed and how it moves. Can you confirm the following for the hosted Redwood API and for Dedicated/Private options: 

1) Primary processing regions (US/EU/APAC) and where ephemeral inference caches and logs reside.
2) Any cross-border transfers that occur (e.g., between EU and US) for indexing, telemetry, or billing.
3) Subprocessors used (cloud providers, telemetry, monitoring) and their regions.
4) Data retention defaults and exact deletion behavior once a customer requests purge — how long until tokens/backups/KV cache are removed?
5) Are we able to scope processing to EU-only for PII-heavy workloads (no replication to US)?

If you have a simple diagram and subprocessor list you can send that would help the review. Also, let me know if you prefer a short technical call — security folks want to be on.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of InfoSec, LedgerWorks
security@ledgerworks.com
message_2_subject: Re: Clarify processing regions, transit paths, and deletion policy for LedgerWorks POC
message_2_body:
Hi Samir — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a concise data-flow diagram and our current subprocessor roster (CSV) to speed review (see attachments). High-level answers below; happy to jump on a 30-minute call to walk through specifics with your security team.

- Processing regions: Hosted API endpoints are deployed regionally. For EU-only residency we run inference in eu-west1 (GCP) or eu-central1 (AWS by request) depending on capacity. Default hosted customers are routed to the nearest region by latency policy (us / eu / apac).

- Ephemeral caches & logs: Inference KV cache and prefix caches are stored in the same region as the inference node (no default cross-region replication). Request-level telemetry (aggregated metrics) is replicated to a centralized analytics cluster for operational monitoring (this is pseudonymized and telemetry-only).

- Cross-border transfers: By default, telemetry aggregates and billing metadata may traverse regions for processing (e.g., billing in us-east). For customers requiring EU-only, our Hosted option can be configured to restrict routing and telemetry to EU-only endpoints — see Dedicated/Private below.

- Subprocessors: See attached CSV with providers and primary processing regions. Short list: AWS (us-east-1, eu-west-1), GCP (europe-west1), Datadog (metrics - US/EU), Sentry (error monitoring - EU/US), Auth0 (identity). If you need us to route logs to an EU-only logging provider we can arrange that on Dedicated/Private.

- Retention & deletion: Default retention for request, prompt, and response material in Hosted: 30 days for short-term caching (used for KV/prefix), 180 days for aggregated logs/metrics. When a customer requests deletion via API or support ticket: we delete primary inference logs and cached prompt/response shards within 30 days; backups and long-term analytics (if retained for billing/metrics) are scrubbed within 90 days unless legal hold applies. For Dedicated/Private customers you can set stricter retention (including immediate log purge on request) and bring-your-own KMS.

- EU-only option: Yes — Dedicated and Private deployments support an EU-only processing posture (no cross-border replication). For Hosted, we offer an EU residency plan that minimizes transfer but requires a contractual addendum for strict no-transfer guarantees.

Next steps: I can (1) share the CSV/diagram now (attached), (2) schedule a quick call — Calendly link here: https://calendly.com/aditya-rao/redwood-technical-review, or (3) loop in our compliance lead if you want the legal addendum template.

Cheers,
Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-data-flow-diagram-20261105.png, subprocessors-20261105.csv
message_3_subject: Re: Clarify processing regions, transit paths, and deletion policy for LedgerWorks POC
message_3_body:
Hi Samir — looping in Neha from Product/Privacy to add a few precise SLA items and to confirm edge cases. Quick clarifications: 

- Deletion SLA: For Hosted customers who request data deletion we commit to removing customer prompt/response records and KV cache entries from the active serving tier within 30 days. Secondary backups are purged within 90 days; customers can request acceleration for critical PII via our support/legal review (we provide an excerpted audit trail).

- Backups & snapshots: Regular storage snapshots exist for disaster recovery. Those are typically retained for a short window (90 days max) and are encrypted. We document timeline and can provide attestation for POC.

- Logs & billing metadata: We separate personally-identifiable content from operational logs; billing metadata (usage totals) may be processed in US-based billing pipelines. If LedgerWorks requires EU billing-only processing, we can discuss routing and contractual terms.

- Dedicated/Private: These deployments support (a) customer-managed VPC, (b) BYOK/BYOK-HSM, and (c) no external telemetry export. In Private mode you retain control of all outbound network egress rules — effectively preventing cross-border transfer.

- Subprocessor notes: The attached CSV lists each subprocessors' declared locations and whether they act on behalf of Redwood as a data processor. For any that touch EU personal data we have Data Processing Agreements executed by default; we can provide SCCs and SOC2 reports on request.

I’ve redlined a few items in the supplied diagram and subprocessor list (see Drive link). If you sign off on a short call, Neha and I will share the contractual addendum that covers residency constraints.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

1) Please share SOC2 Type II (most recent) and the signed SCCs if possible.
2) Can you confirm the fastest possible timeline to accelerate deletion of PII from backups (our compliance team sometimes requires <30 days for particular classes of data)?
3) Would you be able to provide an EU-only Hosted pilot (billing/telemetry excluded) or do we need Dedicated for full EU-only assurances?

If you can attach the SOC2 and SCCs here or a secure drive link, I’ll circulate within LedgerWorks. I’ve booked a 30-minute slot on Aditya’s Calendly for Wednesday morning to review technical specifics.

Samir
